definitions.explanation: Ground that is frozen, either temporarily in winter or permanently in cold regions. Often used in the compound 永久凍土 (permafrost).

examples.japanese: {永久|えいきゅう}{凍土|とうど}が{溶|と}けている。
{北極|ほっきょく}には{広大|こうだい}な{凍土|とうど}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
examples.english: Vast stretches of frozen ground spread across the Arctic.

examples.japanese: {地球|ちきゅう}{温暖化|おんだんか}で{永久|えいきゅう}{凍土|とうど}が{急速|きゅうそく}に{減|へ}っている。
examples.english: Due to global warming, permafrost is rapidly decreasing.

notes:
{凍土|とうど} refers to ground or soil that is frozen, whether seasonally or permanently. In everyday Japanese, it most often appears in the compound {永久|えいきゅう}{凍土|とうど} (permafrost), particularly in discussions of climate change and Arctic environments.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {凍土|とうど}が{溶|と}ける (frozen ground melts)
- {凍土|とうど}が{広|ひろ}がる (frozen ground extends)
- {凍土|とうど}が{減|へ}る (frozen ground decreases)
- {凍土|とうど}{地帯|ちたい} (frozen ground zone)

COMPOUNDS:
- {永久|えいきゅう}{凍土|とうど} (permafrost — permanently frozen ground)
- {凍土|とうど}{壁|へき} (frozen soil wall — used in construction to block groundwater)

USAGE:
- Most commonly encountered in the compound {永久|えいきゅう}{凍土|とうど}
- Used in geography, environmental science, and climate change discussions
- The kanji {凍|とう} means "freeze" and {土|ど} means "earth/soil"
